chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The people have been commanded to come to these stones, so they perform Tawaf by them; then they should come to us, informing us of their Wilayah, and presenting to us their support.
ai.seo_question: What is the connection between Hajj rituals and allegiance to the Imams in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Shia concept of 'Hajj al-Imam', where the physical pilgrimage to the Ka'bah is incomplete without the subsequent Ziyarah to the Imams, who serve as the spiritual and political successors of the Prophet. By presenting their 'Nasr' (support/victory) to the Imams, pilgrims affirm the continuity of divine authority, transforming the ritual into an act of political and spiritual allegiance. This linkage highlights the Imams' role as the ultimate destination of worship, bridging the gap between the House of God and the House of the Prophet.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘But rather, the people have been Commanded that they should come to these rocks, so they would be performing Tawaaf by these. Then they should be coming to usasws, and informing usasws of their Wilayah, and they should be presenting to usasws their support’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
People are commanded to come to these stones, perform Tawaf, thereafter come to us to inform us of their acceptance of our Divine Authority and offer us their support. ‘“
